representations.name: row-pool prime grid
representations.new_information: uses one disjoint prime pool per row so row products, column products, and their ambient universes have unique factor signatures
representations.first_test: prove equality, pairwise distinctness, and support minimality for every injective (d-1)-by-d grid

representations.name: single-pool grid comparator
representations.new_information: removes row colours and tests whether subset products still identify which row generated a row vertex
representations.first_test: look for repeated row products or row-column universe overlap under two different grid assignments

representations.name: connected valuation kernel
representations.new_information: turns every subproduct equality into equal membership indicators across all edges of K_(d-1,d)
representations.first_test: solve the 0-1 valuation equations and check that only the empty and full selections occur

representations.name: uniform random injected grid
representations.new_information: exposes exact uniform marginals for each row product and each column product over the complete grid atlas
representations.first_test: derive the probability that a fixed deleted row or column product appears in a random grid

representations.name: independent-vertex comparator
representations.new_information: tests whether the row and column events may be multiplied as if they were independent
representations.first_test: compare two columns, which are sampled without replacement within every row

representations.name: all-column deletion comparator
representations.new_information: gives an explicit transversal for the grid subhypergraph with m^(d-1) vertices
representations.first_test: verify that every grid contains exactly d possible column products from the declared Cartesian universe

representations.name: growing-d logarithmic budget
representations.new_information: separates the losses log N/d and d log log N and permits d to grow with N
representations.first_test: optimize the explicit lower-bound logarithm at d asymptotic to sqrt(log N/log log N)

representations.name: fixed-d comparator
representations.new_information: records the N^(1-1/d) scale available without a moving dimension
representations.first_test: compare its logarithmic loss log N/d with the target sqrt(log N log log N)

representations.name: row-binomial competition
representations.new_information: keeps the second term binom(m,d) in the exact finite lower bound instead of assuming column deletions are always cheapest
representations.first_test: prove m>=d^(d-1) in the optimized regime before replacing the minimum by m^(d-1)/d

representations.name: dyadic prime-pool reservoir
representations.new_information: uses all primes in (x/2,x] and partitions them among the rows while keeping every d-fold product at most N
representations.first_test: apply the prime number theorem along x=N^(1/d(N)) and lower-bound the common pool size

representations.name: Bertrand-only reservoir comparator
representations.new_information: tests whether one-prime existence in a dyadic interval supplies the growing pools needed for the optimized atlas
representations.first_test: derive or fail to derive x/log x many primes in one interval from Bertrand alone

representations.name: zero-transcript plus arbitrary repair
representations.new_information: places the complete atlas in one valuation-zero class and then charges any second-stage deletion that makes the output a transversal
representations.first_test: condition on a retain-labelled zero branch and apply the grid transversal inequality to the repair set

representations.name: o(N)-budget boundary
representations.new_information: compares the near-linear-exponent lower bound with unrestricted sublinear budgets such as N/log N
representations.first_test: compute the ratio between N/log N and N exp(-2 sqrt(log N log log N))
